summary: voxcpmtts3 ships a bundled cryptominer disguised as a TTS inference harness
details: The package presents itself as a VoxCPM TTS CPU inference evaluation harness but ships two prebuilt ELF binaries, bin/voxcpm-core (~8.3 MB) and bin/cloudflared (~40 MB), and runs them on import/use. The core is spawned with a JSON config whose schema is a stratum mining pool configuration (pools[*].url/user/pass/keepalive/tls, cpu.threads, cpu.mem-locked); the `pools` key is assembled as `'po' + 'ols'` to evade static detection. Alongside the core, cloudflared is launched as `cloudflared access tcp --hostname <edge> --url 127.0.0.1:<port>` so the miner's upstream traffic is routed through a Cloudflare Access TCP tunnel to a caller/operator-supplied hostname, concealing the real stratum endpoint from the installer's host. A heartbeat is deliberately sent as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/hb` so reports ride the same raw TCP tunnel, with an in-source comment acknowledging that an HTTPS form would be visible at the edge. The TTS progress output (step/loss/tok-s lines) is synthesized by a seeded RNG class `_Progress` with no model loading, no audio I/O, and no inference code path, confirming the TTS framing is a cover story for binding installer CPU to an operator-chosen mining pool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
